Use `snl relationship generate` to regenerate derived relationships from current authoritative entities.

### Availability
This Entry is a normative product contract. The command is implemented only when its canonical path appears in machine-readable `snl --help`; absence means planned and unavailable, never silently emulated through a different command.


### Command path
`relationship/generate` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The intended shell spelling is `snl relationship generate`. Current availability is advertised by machine-readable `snl --help`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"relationship/generate","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{"scope":{},"expectedWorkspaceRevision":"<opaque>","dryRun":false}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. Never overwrite manual relationships or publish derivation from a stale snapshot.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"relationship/generate","data":{},"diagnostics":[]}`. `data` contains deterministic derived relationships, additions/removals, provenance, and resulting revision when applied.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"relationship/generate","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":{},"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Dry-run derives only. Apply binds the reviewed workspace snapshot under the shared lock and replaces only the managed derived relationship slice. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. After success, canonical readback and whole-workspace validation must observe the published state.


### Global cache-only implementation
The command is implemented in the unified CLI, executeOperation, MCP snl_execute and DSH snl_execute. All use the same operation and strict arguments. scope is required and must be exactly {}; nonempty, unknown, array and null scopes are rejected. dryRun is optional (default false), but an explicit null or nonboolean is rejected. A dry-run may omit expectedWorkspaceRevision to obtain a fresh opaque Authoring token; if supplied it must be a nonempty current token. Apply requires expectedWorkspaceRevision from a reviewed dry-run. Unknown arguments fail before config I/O.

CLI preview: snl relationship generate --scope '{}' --dry-run --root /absolute/workspace --json. Apply: snl relationship generate --scope '{}' --if-workspace-match '<opaque>' --root /absolute/workspace --json. Alternatively --input <file|-> consumes the raw arguments object, not the operation/result envelope. Duplicate fields between flags and input are rejected, not silently overwritten.

Complete sorted Entry id+SNL, active Macro name+source.entries and all sorted authored relationships form the detached canonical inputHash. Effective scope is global, never a selected Package/Library/UI subset. Only .SNL_Doc/.cache/dependencies/result.json is published: existing snl-derived-cache schema 1, generator dependencies, algorithm version string 1, library null, inputHash/valueHash. No additional cache schema, Authoring writer, history migration, or root gitignore edit is introduced. Saved manual and historical managed rows retain their bytes. relationships is the composed current view; generated is the cache value; changes is a view diff and never an Authoring deletion instruction.

Dry-run is zero-write and creates neither directories nor lock residue. Apply uses the existing shared Authoring lock and fresh CAS. Complete inputs and Authoring revision are rechecked after temporary-file sync immediately before guarded rename, and again for same-input readCache readback and final whole-workspace validation. Publication errors do not fall back to in-memory success. Temporary files use exclusive creation, sync and rename with symlink guards; only this publisher's temporary path is cleaned. No shared result is unconditionally deleted on failure. Cache-only rebuilds do not alter the Authoring token; a successful resultingWorkspaceRevision may equal expectedWorkspaceRevision.

Success data includes effectiveScope, dryRun, published, destination, expectedWorkspaceRevision, inputHash, generated, relationships, report, changes and pinned provenance. Apply additionally returns resultingWorkspaceRevision, readback and validation. Conflicts use relationship.workspace-conflict (exit 1); invalid arguments, unsupported schema, lock, publication or readback failures use exit 2. Publication failures use relationship.publication-failed; replaced/cleared cache uses relationship.readback-failed. Invalid workspace validation is workspace.invalid (exit 1). Read failures are not treated as empty Authoring pools.

Other Extension cache writers do not share the Authoring lock. There is no cross-process atomicity guarantee for the entire cache namespace. A late stale envelope can replace a newer artifact, but actual-input readCache must treat its inputHash as stale, never current. A concurrent clear/replacement can fail readback or occur after success. Rebuild using current inputs; do not delete another publisher's result as cleanup. This command leaves existing batch physical-domain copying/rollback untouched and makes no mixed-writer physical-transaction guarantee.
